text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports uncontrolled blood sugar, with home readings in the 300s.
- history of present illness: the patient has noticed blood sugar gradually creeping up at home. Diet is reportedly unchanged, with sugar coming mainly from fruit. Reflux has improved on protonix. History of congestive heart failure, with no recent weight gain reported. Prior right rotator cuff issue is now much better. Right knee pain noticed on questioning. Transient nausea a few days ago, attributed to car travel.
- physical examination: thyroid mildly enlarged. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft. Right knee with erythema and an insect bite with fluctuance. Right lower extremity edema. Vital signs normal. Labs: elevated Lyme titer, positive rapid strep.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: hyperglycemia, right knee joint pain, transient nausea. Denies fever, chills, and dysuria.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day for 10 days.
- follow-up instructions: Lyme western blot PCR ordered; nurse to arrange tests; patient to call if anything changes.
